notes.story: Trend scout item 1: 'Project Anchor' hoax claiming Earth would lose gravity for 7 seconds at 14:33 UTC on 12 Aug 2026, citing a fake leaked '$89 billion NASA document'. It spread from January 2026 and was debunked in January and again around the date.
notes.fact_check: research/08-fact-check-wave3.md row 13, GREEN (framing AMBER), filed 2026-09-28. Applied.
sources: Newsweek, NASA senior science communicator Karen Fox: the hoax 'comes around every year' (URL to be added by the Fact-Checker; not given in row 13)
notes.journal: Not a paper. NASA and fact-checker debunks, January and August 2026.
caveats_on_screen: Physics claims kept generic: gravity is a property of mass, cannot be switched off, has no schedule. NASA's own line is quoted once.
States that no such NASA document has ever been produced and that NASA called it false and fact-checkers found no trace of it in NASA's records. No 'observatory officials' (unverified).
The hoax's own figures ($89 billion, 7 seconds, 14:33 UTC, November 2024 leak, colliding black holes) appear only inside the quoted claim.

The real 12 August total solar eclipse is the coincidence that helped the hoax spread; visibility (Spain, Iceland, Greenland, a corner of Portugal) and totality 16:58 to 18:34 UTC, up to 2 min 18 s, are from fact-check row 13.

caption:
Earth did not lose gravity for 7 seconds on 12 August 2026. The 'Project Anchor' posts cited a leaked '$89 billion NASA document' that no one has ever produced. Gravity is a property of mass; it has no off switch. NASA and fact-checkers debunked it. The real event that day was a total solar eclipse. Sources on slide 8.

#debunk #physics #gravity #science #factcheck

slides.title: No, Earth did not lose gravity for *7 seconds*
slides.sub: The 'Project Anchor' hoax about 12 August 2026, and what physics actually says.

slides.title: A leaked "$89 billion NASA document" predicted a 7-second gravity loss
slides.body: At 14:33 UTC on 12 August 2026, blamed on "intersecting gravitational waves from colliding black holes". It spread across TikTok, Facebook, Instagram, X and Reddit.

slides.myth: Gravity can switch off for 7 seconds
slides.fact: Gravity is a property of mass. It cannot be switched off.
slides.body: As long as Earth has mass, Earth has gravity. There is no off switch and no schedule. NASA spokesperson, January 2026: "Earth's gravity, or total gravitational force, is determined by its mass."

slides.title: No such NASA document has ever been *produced*
slides.body: NASA called it false; fact-checkers found no trace of it in NASA's records.

slides.title: Three ingredients of a viral hoax
items: A **specific date and time**: 14:33 UTC, 12 August
A fake **leaked document** with a huge price tag for credibility
A **real event** the same day: a total solar eclipse

slides.title: There *was* a total solar eclipse on 12 August
slides.body: Seen from Spain, Iceland, Greenland and a corner of Portugal. Totality 16:58 to 18:34 UTC, up to 2 min 18 s. The hoax's 14:33 UTC was two hours before the eclipse even began. Real, spectacular, and not a gravity switch.

slides.title: How to spot the next one
items: Exact date, exact time, huge dollar figure: **be suspicious**
Check the agency's own website for the document
Ask what law of physics would have to break
Snopes fact check (rating: False; NASA's statement by email): https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/nasa-project-anchor-earth-gravity/
Newsweek, NASA's Karen Fox: the hoax 'comes around every year'
